extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry and experts in Inter-Universal Teichmüller (IUT) theory
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition and formalization of the construction and properties of log-links and log-theta-lattices in Mochizuki's IUT framework, culminating in bi-coricity/bi-core results for Gaussian log-theta-lattices. Targets structural compatibility, (non-)commutativity, and functorial algorithms across vertical/horizontal links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplicative indeterminacy → additive indeterminacy via log
rubrics_metrics.description: Any multiplicative indeterminacy with respect to the action on O_k^× of some subgroup H ⊆ O_k^× at some “•” of the diagram Γ gives rise to an additive indeterminacy with respect to the action of log_k(H) on the copy of “O_k” that corresponds to the subsequent “•” of the diagram Γ. In particular, if H consists of roots of unity, then log_k(H) = {0}, so the resulting additive indeterminacy ceases to exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this principle when tracking how quotienting by multiplicative actions produces additive ambiguities after applying logarithms; roots of unity eliminate the additive indeterminacy. This observation is applied later (e.g., §3) in contexts of canonical splittings and rigidity properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global arithmetic line bundles: multiplicative translates and indeterminacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Considering global arithmetic line bundles amounts to considering multiplicative translates by f ∈ F^×_mod of the product of the various O_k^× as v ranges over V. Such translates are disjoint except when f is a unit at all v ∈ V, which corresponds precisely to f being a root of unity. Quotients by this multiplicative action give rise to an additive indeterminacy by 'logarithms of roots of unity' at subsequent nodes; at v ∈ V_non the resulting additive indeterminacy ceases, while at v ∈ V_arc the indeterminacy corresponds to taking quotients of copies of O_k^× by some finite subgroup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply elementary algebraic number theory to decide when multiplicative translates collide; track whether f is unit everywhere (root of unity) to predict additive indeterminacy. Use when forming global objects and taking quotients in §3 constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Log-wall: incompatibility of the log-link with ring homomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: The log-link gp_log(†F_v) does not arise from a ring homomorphism between the rings in question; this incompatibility between ring structures on either side of the log-link is the 'log-wall'. Consequently, it is not possible a priori to transport objects whose structure depends on ring structures via the log-link by invoking 'transport of structure'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume scheme-theoretic basepoints or ring-structure-dependent constructions can be carried across a log-link. Replace ring-dependent notions by structures manifestly compatible with the log-link (see D-prime-strips, etale-like structures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Only D-prime-strip (abstract topological/Aut-holomorphic structures) compatible with log-link
rubrics_metrics.description: The only structure manifestly compatible with the log-link are the associated D-prime-strips — i.e., the abstract topological groups (isomorphic to 'Π_v' at v ∈ V_non) and abstract Aut-holomorphic spaces (isomorphic to 'U_v' at v ∈ V_arc).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When constructing or transporting data across a log-link, work with D-prime-strip type objects (abstract topological/Aut-holomorphic) rather than scheme-theoretic/ring-structure dependent objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structures incompatible with the log-wall
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of structures incompatible with the log-wall include (a) the additive structure on the image of the Kummer map, and (b) in birational situations, the datum of the collection of closed points that determines the affine curve (i.e., scheme-theoretic basepoint data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid relying on additive Kummer-image structures or data determined essentially by schemes/rings when working across the log-wall; such data will not transfer compatibly via log-links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triangular compatibility obstruction for outer surjections
rubrics_metrics.description: In situations replacing Π_v by the absolute Galois group Π_birat of the function field (birational situation), the datum of particular outer surjections (kernels Δ_birat, Δ_v and their outer G_v-actions) — which depends essentially on scheme/ring structures — fails to be compatible with the log-link. This reflects an obstruction of 'triangular compatibility between independent indeterminacies'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect that trying to relate birational and affine geometric fundamental groups via log-links is obstructed by incompatibility of scheme-dependent outer surjections; model reasoning should avoid such scheme-dependent identifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-anabelian construction algorithms must be invariant (coric) under log-action
rubrics_metrics.description: Mono-anabelian construction algorithms in the context of the log-link should be understood as algorithms whose dependence on data arising from fixed ring/scheme-theoretic reference models is 'invariant', or 'coric', with respect to the action of log on such models. This is formulated via notions such as observables, families of homotopies, and telecores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing algorithms, ensure their outputs are invariant under the relevant log-indeterminacies; use the formal apparatus (observables, homotopies, telecores) to certify coricity as in AbsTopIII §3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of the log-Link (Proposition 1.3 (i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix an isomorphism Ξ : †HT D-Θ±ellNF → ‡HT D-Θ±ellNF of D-Θ±ellNF-Hodge theaters. For each F-prime-strip †F appearing in the Θ- and Θ±-bridges of †HT Θ±ellNF, the poly-isomorphism determined by Ξ between associated D-prime-strips uniquely determines a poly-isomorphism log(†F) → log→ ‡F, hence a log-link. The log-link from †HT Θ±ellNF to ‡HT Θ±ellNF is the collection of data consisting of Ξ together with the collection of these log-links for all F-prime-strips; when Ξ is a poly-isomorphism, the resulting collection is the full log-link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To produce a log-link, begin with a (poly-)isomorphism of the underlying D-theaters and then extract the induced poly-isomorphisms on constituent F-prime-strips; aggregate these to form the (full) log-link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coricity of log-links (Proposition 1.3 (ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any log-link †HT Θ±ellNF log→ ‡HT Θ±ellNF induces (and may be thought of as 'lying over') a (poly-)isomorphism †HT D-Θ±ellNF → ‡HT D-Θ±ellNF of D-Θ±ellNF-Hodge theaters — i.e., log-links are coric with respect to the underlying D-theaters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When verifying a constructed log-link, check that it corresponds to an induced (poly-)isomorphism on the D-side; coricity is essential for subsequent functorial constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further properties of log-links: compatibility list (Proposition 1.3 (iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each log-link satisfies properties corresponding to Proposition 1.2, (ii)–(ix), concerning simultaneous compatibility with ring structures and log-volumes, Kummer theory, and log-shells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that any claimed log-link meets the specified compatibility requirements (ring/log-volume behavior, Kummer compatibilities, log-shell inclusion properties) enumerated in the referenced Proposition 1.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frobenius-picture: infinite chain and Z-translation symmetry (Proposition 1.3 (iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: A bi-infinite sequence of distinct Θ±ellNF-Hodge theaters indexed by Z with full log-links between successive terms induces an infinite chain of log-linked theaters and associated full poly-isomorphisms on D-theaters. The oriented graph representing this chain admits a natural Z-action (translation symmetry) which fixes the 'core' but does not admit arbitrary permutation symmetries (e.g., cannot swap adjacent vertices while fixing others).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this picture to reason about periodic/translation symmetries and invariance properties; do not assume richer symmetry groups than the stated Z-translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Log-theta-lattice: definition and Gaussian/non-Gaussian distinction (Definition 1.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: A log-theta-lattice is a diagram whose vertical arrows are full log-links and whose horizontal arrows are the Θ×μ- and Θ×μ_gau-links of IUTchII Corollary 4.10, (iii). The log-theta-lattice involving Θ×μ-links is called non-Gaussian; the one involving Θ×μ_gau-links is called Gaussian. Symbolically, it is represented by an oriented grid where •'s correspond to n,m HT Θ±ellNF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When building or referring to such lattices, explicitly record whether horizontals are Θ×μ or Θ×μ_gau to determine Gaussian status; verticals should be full log-links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noncommutativity of squares in log-theta-lattices
rubrics_metrics.description: The various squares in each log-theta-lattice are far from being commutative. Vertical arrows are constructed using logarithms at v ∈ V (defined by power series depending on local ring structures), while horizontal Θ×μ- and Θ×μ_gau-links are incompatible with these local ring structures in an essential way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume square-commutativity when composing vertical and horizontal arrows; account for noncommutativity in proofs and constructions (order matters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intertwining of horizontal and vertical arrows obligates vertical steps; vertical-core invariance needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Executing a horizontal arrow of the log-theta-lattice obligates a subsequent execution of a vertical arrow in order to avail oneself of log-shell theory and to realize multiradial representations. Because of noncommutativity, multiradiality (simultaneous compatibility with arithmetic holomorphic structures on both sides of a horizontal arrow) can only be realized if one works with objects invariant with respect to the vertical Z-action — i.e., with 'vertical cores' of the lattice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design objects and arguments to be vertical-core invariant when attempting multiradial constructions; plan compositions so horizontals are followed by appropriate vertical steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analogy with p-adic Teichmüller theory: horizontals vs verticals
rubrics_metrics.description: Horizontal arrows of the log-theta-lattice correspond to the mixed-characteristic extension structure of a ring of Witt vectors (transition from p^n Z / p^{n+1} Z to p^{n-1}Z / p^n Z), while vertical arrows correspond to the Frobenius morphism in positive characteristic. The intertwining of horizontals and verticals in the lattice is the analogue of the intertwining between Witt-vector extension structure and Frobenius in classical p-adic theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the analogy to guide intuition and to import heuristics from p-adic Teichmüller theory, but verify that technical compatibility conditions in IUT are satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Horizontal linking data subject to (Z^×)-indeterminacy; horizontals as universal coverings of loops
rubrics_metrics.description: Horizontal linking data (the 'O^×_μ's at v ∈ V_non) is subject to a Z^×-indeterminacy which obliterates the arithmetic holomorphic structure associated to a vertical line. Forcing horizontals to induce isomorphisms of Π_v rigidifies the structure but then the action of nontrivial elements of Z^× obliterates that common structure; one must consider paths recording sequences of 'Π_v-rigidifying' and 'Z^×-indeterminacy' operations. Horizontals amount effectively to universal covering spaces of these loops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When attempting to rigidify horizontals, track Z^×-indeterminacy operations explicitly (paths/unraveling) rather than assuming a single rigid arithmetic holomorphic structure persists across actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertical Coricity of Gaussian log-theta-lattice (Theorem 1.5 (i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The vertical arrows of a Gaussian log-theta-lattice induce full poly-isomorphisms between the respective associated D-Θ±ellNF-Hodge theaters (holding n fixed and varying m).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In Gaussian lattices, verify vertical arrows give full poly-isomorphisms on D-theaters; this underlies many descent and functorial algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Horizontal Coricity of Gaussian log-theta-lattice (Theorem 1.5 (ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The horizontal arrows of a Gaussian log-theta-lattice induce full poly-isomorphisms between the respective associated F^×_μ-prime-strips (holding m fixed and varying n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In Gaussian lattices, check horizontals yield full poly-isomorphisms of F^×_μ-prime-strips; combine with vertical coricity when reason about bi-directional invariants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bi-coric F^×_μ-prime-strips and functorial construction (Theorem 1.5 (iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each pair n,m ∈ Z, functorial algorithms in the associated D-prime-strips produce natural identifications yielding an F^×-prime-strip and associated F^×_μ-prime-strips; composing poly-isomorphisms yields that the F^×_μ-prime-strip 'n,mF' (up to a certain class of isomorphisms) is an invariant — called 'bi-coric' — of both horizontal and vertical arrows. Kummer isomorphisms determine maps compatible with these poly-isomorphisms and with ×μ-Kummer structures at v ∈ V_non and with analogous compatibilities at v ∈ V_arc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When asserting an object is bi-coric, produce the indicated functorial algorithms and Kummer-compatible identifications; check compatibility with both horizontal and vertical poly-isomorphisms and local Kummer structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bi-coric mono-analytic log-shells (Theorem 1.5 (iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: The poly-isomorphisms constituting bi-coricity induce poly-isomorphisms between certain inclusions I_{n,m}^{D} ⊆ log(n,m^D) and corresponding I_{n,m}^{F^×_μ} ⊆ log(F^×_μ(n,m^D)), and one obtains holomorphic log-shells with enveloping 'log(-)' pairs. These isomorphisms are compatible with natural poly-isomorphisms from Proposition 1.2 (viii) and are induced by the Kummer isomorphisms of (iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To exhibit bi-coric log-shells, construct the indicated inclusions and show the induced poly-isomorphisms are compatible with the Kummer maps and Proposition 1.2 (viii) identifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bi-coric mono-analytic global realiﬁed Frobenioids (Theorem 1.5 (v))
rubrics_metrics.description: The poly-isomorphisms of D-prime-strips induced by the full poly-isomorphisms (i),(ii) produce isomorphisms of collections of data — a Frobenioid, a bijection, and a collection of isomorphisms of topological monoids indexed by V — compatible (relative to horizontal arrows) with R_{>0}-orbits of isomorphisms obtained by functorial algorithms from IUTchII Corollary 4.6 and 4.10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When constructing global realized Frobenioids, assemble the Frobenioid, bijection, and local monoid isomorphisms coherently and verify compatibility with horizontal poly-isomorphisms and the R_{>0}-orbit behavior coming from the referenced algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conjugate synchronization is essential for bi-coricity (descent from label-dependent to label-independent data)
rubrics_metrics.description: The theory of conjugate synchronization (IUTchII Corollaries 4.5, 4.6) provides a descent mechanism turning label-dependent data (labels t ∈ LabCusp±) into label-independent data, which is essential in constructing horizontally coric objects. Conjugate synchronization, together with Kummer isomorphisms, is crucial to construct vertically coric objects as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to bypass conjugate synchronization in building bi-coric objects; if trying to simplify, explicitly account for loss of label-independence and Kummer compatibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naive diagonal-conjugacy approach fails due to nonabelian commutator factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Attempting to replace conjugate synchronization by identifying a diagonal embedding G → G×...×G with its (G×...×G)-conjugates forces identifications (g,g) ∼ (g,hgh^{-1}) = (g,[h,g]·g), which identifies (g,g) with (g,g) times (1,[h,g]). This is incompatible with the requirement that factors like (1,[h,g]) correspond to distinct elements at distinct components (needed to represent distinct Galois-theoretic Kummer classes); the incompatibility stems from the highly nonabelian nature of G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid treating diagonal embeddings up to ambient conjugacy as a substitute for conjugate synchronization when distinct Kummer classes at components must be preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combinatorial resemblance of conjugate and label synchronization
rubrics_metrics.description: At a combinatorial level, conjugate synchronization is reminiscent of label synchronization: both may be viewed as combinatorial representations of the arithmetic holomorphic structure associated to a single vertical line of the log-theta-lattice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this combinatorial viewpoint to understand the role of synchronization mechanisms, but remember the deeper Kummer/ coricity/ functorial algorithmic content is necessary for the formal constructions.
